# `starhermit:audio`

Engine **1.40.0** (host API 1.40), the latest release. Generated from the release's `starhermit.d.ts`; `starhermit types` writes the same file into your game. [All modules](index.md).

```ts
import { … } from "starhermit:audio";
```

Two ways to make sound, both mixed by the engine on the player's volume buses (Options › Audio): clip playback for sound effects and music, and a synthesis graph in the Web Audio model (`context`). The game's sound is muted while the window is unfocused when the player asked for that. In checks (`--check`, `--render-check`) the game plays silently on the checks' simulated clock, as `frame().time` does: sounds' and streams' ends, a stream's `position`, sources' `ended` and `currentTime` follow the frames played, not real time, so a play script sees them at the same frames in every run.

### Bus

*type*

```ts
export type Bus = "music" | "effects" | "interface";
```

The player's volume group a sound plays in.

## Clips

### AudioClip

*class*

Decoded samples registered with the mixer. A game holds at most `engine.limits.audio_clips` clips (128 by default; a manifest may raise it up to 1,024 since API\_MINOR 18) and min(`audio_mib`, 64 MiB) of clip data (RangeError). Clips reach the mixer in the order they were made, a few at a time; in a browser they wait for its audio, which starts with the player's first press, so load them all at the start. One the mixer could not make is logged as a warning, and `play` of it then throws an Error saying why.

```ts
export class AudioClip { … }
```

- `#private;`
- `private constructor();`

- `readonly duration: number;`

  Seconds.

- `readonly sampleRate: number;`
- `readonly channels: number;`

- `dispose(): void;`

  Releases it and stops its sounds; using it afterwards throws a TypeError.

### loadClip

*function*

```ts
export function loadClip(path: string): Promise<AudioClip>;
```

Decodes a package file (WAV, Ogg Vorbis, Ogg Opus), read without waiting for it (see `PackageFiles`). Rejects with a TypeError for a bad path, `NotFoundError`, `NetworkError` when the file could not be had, `EncodingError` for data it cannot decode, RangeError past the budget or with 128 decodes already waiting.

### createClip

*function*

```ts
export function createClip(channels: readonly Float32Array[], sampleRate: number): AudioClip;
```

From samples (−1..1): one array per channel (1–8), 8–192 kHz; non-finite samples throw a TypeError.

```ts
export function createClip(buffer: AudioBuffer): AudioClip;
```

Since API\_MINOR 37 (`OFFLINE_AUDIO_MINOR`; a TypeError before): a clip of an AudioBuffer's samples at its rate (8–192 kHz, else a RangeError), copied natively: what `OfflineAudioContext`'s `startRendering()` gives becomes a clip to `play` (with `loop`) without a sample passing through script.

### PlayOptions

*interface*

```ts
export interface PlayOptions { … }
```

- `gain?: number;`

  0–16 (default 1).

- `pitch?: number;`

  Playback-rate multiplier, 0.125–8 (default 1).

- `pan?: number;`

  −1 (left) .. 1 (right); omitted: the clip's own channels.

- `loop?: boolean;`

- `bus?: Bus;`

  Default `"effects"`.

- `when?: number;`

  Since API\_MINOR 37 (`SCHEDULED_PLAY_MINOR`; ignored before): when it starts, in seconds of `context.currentTime`, as Web Audio's `start(when)`: `play(clip, { when: context.currentTime + 0.5 })` starts half a second from now, on the very frame a graph source started at the same time does; a time already past (or omitted) starts at once. TypeError when not finite, RangeError below 0. Until then the sound is `playing` and silent; its end (and `onEnded`) comes that much later.

- `priority?: number;`

  Since API\_MINOR 37 (`SOUND_BANK_MINOR`; ignored before): which of the game's sounds the player's sound limit keeps heard, an integer −32,768 to 32,767 (RangeError outside; default 0): past the limit a sound of higher priority displaces a playing one of lower, and equal priorities keep the sounds already heard.

- `caption?: Caption;`

  Since API\_MINOR 37 (`SOUND_CAPTIONS_MINOR`; ignored before): the sound's caption, shown by the runtime as it starts (see `showCaption`), lasting as long as the clip plays at its pitch (a loop's as long as it takes to read). TypeError for a bad caption, before the sound plays.

- `position?: readonly [number, number, number] | { readonly x: number; readonly y: number; readonly z: number };`

  Since API\_MINOR 37 (`SPATIAL_AUDIO_MINOR`; ignored before): a 3D position, `[x, y, z]` or a Vector3: the sound is heard as a Web Audio `PannerNode` at that place would make it against `context.listener` (equal-power panning by its azimuth, its distance model's and cone's gain times `gain`; `pan` is then unused), worked out by the runtime each frame as the sound (`setPosition`) or the listener moves, and glided to by the mixer over a render quantum. A mono clip pans as a mono input, a stereo one by the stereo law. TypeError when not finite. With the player's Spatial sound off it keeps its distance and cone gain and drops only the panning: it plays centered, as a source straight ahead would.

- `orientation?: readonly [number, number, number] | { readonly x: number; readonly y: number; readonly z: number };`

  Which way it faces (default `[1, 0, 0]`), for a cone.

- `panner?: PannerAttributes;`

  The panner's attributes, as `PannerNode`'s (Web Audio's defaults: inverse distance, refDistance 1, maxDistance 10,000, rolloffFactor 1, no cone); RangeError or `InvalidStateError` as there.

### PannerAttributes

*interface*

A `PannerNode`'s attributes (Web Audio's `PannerOptions` but the position and orientation).

```ts
export interface PannerAttributes { … }
```

- `panningModel?: "equalpower" | "HRTF";`

  `"HRTF"` is taken and renders as `"equalpower"` (the engine has no head-related transfer functions).

- `distanceModel?: "linear" | "inverse" | "exponential";`

- `refDistance?: number;`

  At least 0 (RangeError).

- `maxDistance?: number;`

  Above 0 (RangeError); bounds every distance model, as Chromium does: past it a source keeps the gain it has there. (The written Web Audio specification bounds the linear model alone; the engine follows Chrome, where most games and three.js scenes are tuned.)

- `rolloffFactor?: number;`

  At least 0 (RangeError); the linear model clamps it to 1.

- `coneInnerAngle?: number;`

  Degrees (default 360).

- `coneOuterAngle?: number;`

- `coneOuterGain?: number;`

  0–1 (`InvalidStateError` outside), default 0.

### Sound

*class*

A playing clip. Control calls on a finished sound do nothing. `fade`, `setPitch` and `setPan` never throw for the frame's audio operations: the frame keeps the last of each per sound and sends the mixer that one, so setting them every step or many times a frame costs nothing more (before the runtime with host API 1.18 each counted as one of the frame's 1,024 operations, a RangeError past them).

```

- `private constructor();`

  False once it ended (estimated from the clip's length and pitch; a looping sound plays until stopped).

- `stop(): void;`

- `fade(gain: number, seconds: number): void;`

  Ramps the gain over `seconds` (at most 60).

- `setPitch(pitch: number): void;`

### play

*function*

```ts
export function play(clip: AudioClip, options?: PlayOptions): Sound;
```

At most min(`engine.limits.voices`, 256) sounds at once and 1,024 audio operations a frame (plays, a stream's opening, play and pause, and stops and releases, which always go through; a sound's or stream's fade, pitch and pan are not counted); past either a RangeError, which the game can catch. An Error ("the audio clip could not be made: …") for a clip the mixer could not make. Past the player's sound limit (Options › Audio, by default Auto: the device's, never below 16 however loaded the machine) a sound is not refused: it runs on silently and is heard once there is room, as a sound the limit displaced.

## The game's mute (host API 1.37)

The player's Options › Audio volumes stay the player's: a game never changes them. A game's own mute (a M key, a "Sound" toggle in its settings) is a separate flag on the game's buses that combines with them: the game is heard only while neither mutes it. The mute is not kept between runs (keep it in the game's saves or storage and set it again at the start).

### setMuted

*function*

```ts
export function setMuted(muted: boolean): void;
```

Since API\_MINOR 37 (`GAME_MUTE_MINOR`; a TypeError before): mutes or unmutes all of the game's sound (music, effects and interface: clips, streams and the synthesis graph), from the next frame's audio; the graph's clock and sounds' ends run on meanwhile. Not counted among the frame's audio operations.

### isMuted

*function*

```ts
export function isMuted(): boolean;
```

Since API\_MINOR 37: the game's own mute, as last set (false at the start).

### isPlayerMuted

*function*

```ts

```

Since API\_MINOR 37: whether the player's Options › Audio silence the game (its master volume at 0), for a game's own toggle to show; it follows the player's changes.

## Music directors and ambience beds (host API 1.37)

Adaptive music and ambience run by the runtime and the mixer, not the script: a `MusicDirector` plays one state at a time, each state one or more looping stems (clips) started on the same mixer frame, so stems of one length stay in lockstep for good, with each stem's gain following the director's intensity; a state change crossfades on the mixer (the new stems fade in and the old fade out from the same frame, linearly as `linearRampToValueAtTime`, and stop once silent). An `AmbienceBed` keeps looping layers at levels: a layer set above silence starts looping and fades in, one set to 0 fades out and stops. Every change takes effect 0.1 s after `context.currentTime` (on the mixer's frame for that time, so its sounds start and fade together wherever the calls' operations land), and costs the script nothing per frame. Each stem or layer playing is one of the game's sounds (`play`'s limit), and a crossfade holds both states' stems until it ends. Disposing a stem's clip stops its sound. `context` is made with the first director or bed (its clock times the changes).

### Stem

*type*

```ts
export type Stem =
  | AudioClip
  | {
      clip: AudioClip;
      gain?: number;
      intensity?: readonly [number, number];
      until?: readonly [number, number];
    };
```

A stem: a clip, or a clip with its gain (0–16, default 1) and how its gain follows the director's intensity: rising from 0 to 1 as the intensity goes from `intensity[0]` to `intensity[1]` (a step at the first when the two are equal) and falling from 1 to 0 over `until`.

### MusicDirectorOptions

*interface*

```ts
export interface MusicDirectorOptions { … }
```

- ```ts
  states: {
      readonly [state: string]: Stem | readonly Stem[] | { stems: Stem | readonly Stem[]; bar?: number };
    };
  ```

  The states by name (1–64), each its stems (1–16), or `{ stems, bar }` where `bar` is seconds of a bar (0–3600, default 0: none) that changes may align to.

- `crossfade?: number;`

  Seconds of a change's crossfade (0–60, default 2).

- `dwell?: number;`

  Seconds a state plays at least before a change takes effect (0–3600, default 0): a change sooner waits until then, the latest winning (cue hysteresis), unless it is `immediate`.

- `intensity?: number;`

  0–1 (default 1).

- `gain?: number;`

  0–16 (default 1), times each stem's.

- `bus?: Bus;`

  Default `"music"`.

- `priority?: number;`

  As `PlayOptions.priority`, for every stem.

### MusicDirector

*class*

Since API\_MINOR 37 (`MUSIC_DIRECTOR_MINOR`; a TypeError before): music states with crossfades and intensity-layered stems, run natively. TypeError or RangeError for bad options; at most 32 directors and beds at once.

```

- `readonly state: string | null;`

- ```ts
  setState(
      state: string | null,
      options?: { crossfade?: number; align?: "now" | "bar"; immediate?: boolean },

  ```

The state already playing changes nothing. TypeError for an unknown state.

- `setIntensity(intensity: number, seconds?: number): void;`

  Each stem's gain to follow `intensity` (0–1) over `seconds` (0–60, default 1), all from one frame.

  The director's gain (0–16) over `seconds` (default 0.5).

- `stop(seconds?: number): void;`

  Fades out over `seconds` (default the crossfade) and stops: `setState(null, { immediate: true })`.

- `dispose(): void;`

  Stops its sounds at once; later calls throw a TypeError.

## Captions (host API 1.37)

Subtitles for spoken lines and descriptions of sounds that matter to play ("\[Glass shatters\]"), drawn by the runtime over the game, below its own screens: centered near the bottom, at most three at once (the newest at the bottom; a full queue drops its oldest sound description first), each up as long as its sound and as long as its text takes to read, and at least 1.5 s; the same caption again keeps it up longer rather than stacking a copy. They follow the player's Options › Accessibility: Subtitles (spoken lines), Sound captions (descriptions), Caption size (0.5–3) and Caption background (a dark box, else an outline), on by default; a kind turned off is not shown (and goes at once when turned off). Text is the game's, already translated; screen readers read captions as labels.

### Caption

*type*

```ts
export type Caption =
  | string
  | {
      text: string;
      speaker?: string;
      kind?: "sound" | "dialogue";
      duration?: number;
    };
```

A caption: a string is a sound's description (the runtime adds the brackets); an object gives a spoken line (`kind: "dialogue"`, the default with a `speaker`, shown as `speaker: text`) or a description (`"sound"`, the default without one). `text` at most 400 characters, `speaker` 64, `duration` seconds (default the sound's length, or a reading time) 0 or more (else a RangeError).

### showCaption

*function*

```ts
export function showCaption(caption: Caption): void;
```

Since API\_MINOR 37 (`SOUND_CAPTIONS_MINOR`; a TypeError before): shows a caption without a sound of its own (a graph's sound, a stream's line). A frame shows at most 32 captions (the rest are left out). TypeError for a bad caption.

### captionSettings

*function*

```ts
export function captionSettings(): { readonly subtitles: boolean; readonly sounds: boolean };
```

Since API\_MINOR 37 (a TypeError before): the player's caption choices, for a game that draws captions of its own (`subtitles` for spoken lines, `sounds` for descriptions); they follow the player's changes.

## Sound banks (host API 1.37)

### SoundBankOptions

*interface*

`SoundBank`'s options. Jitters are fractions of the base, drawn uniformly each play from the bank's own seeded stream.

```ts
export interface SoundBankOptions { … }
```

- `clips: readonly AudioClip[];`

  The variants, 1 to 64 clips.

- `order?: "random" | "shuffle" | "sequence";`

  `"random"` (default: any variant but the last one played), `"shuffle"` (each once in a seeded order, then again, never the last one first) or `"sequence"` (in turn).

- `gain?: number;`

  0–16 (default 1).

- `gainJitter?: number;`

  0–1 (default 0): each play's gain is `gain × (1 ± gainJitter)`.

- `pitch?: number;`

  0.125–8 (default 1).

- `pitchJitter?: number;`

  0–0.5 (default 0): each play's pitch is `pitch × (1 ± pitchJitter)`.

- `pan?: number;`

  −1..1; omitted: the clips' own channels (unless `panJitter`).

- `panJitter?: number;`

  0–1 (default 0): each play's pan is `pan ± panJitter`.

- `minGap?: number;`

  Seconds of `frame().time` (0–60, default 0): a play sooner after the last one is skipped (`play` returns null), so a burst of hits makes one sound.

- `maxInstances?: number;`

  1–256 (default 256): its sounds at once; past it its oldest sound stops for the new one.

- `priority?: number;`

  As `PlayOptions.priority`.

- `bus?: Bus;`

  Default `"effects"`.

- `panner?: PannerAttributes;`

  Since API\_MINOR 37 (`SPATIAL_AUDIO_MINOR`): the panner of plays with a `position`.

- `caption?: Caption;`

  Since API\_MINOR 37 (`SOUND_CAPTIONS_MINOR`): each play's caption (as `PlayOptions.caption`; a burst of plays shows it once, kept up longer).

- `seed?: number;`

  The stream's seed (a finite number, taken as a 32-bit integer): the same seed and the same plays give the same variants and jitter in every run. Omitted: a different stream each run.

## Streams (host API 1.14)

Long music decoded as it plays: an Ogg Opus (1–2 channels) or Ogg Vorbis (1–8 channels) package or remote file, holding no clip and none of the clip budget. A stream holds at most 3 seconds of decoded audio (2 in the mixer, 1 on its way; in a browser 7, 6 in the mixer, so a page slow to draw does not starve it); a game plays at most 4 at once, each one of its sounds (`play`'s limit). A remote file streams while it arrives when the package's remote index lists its pieces (packaging does, for Ogg files; each 256 KiB piece is checked against its pinned SHA-256 before it is decoded) and stays in the device's cache, so later plays and runs read it from there, offline too; one listed without pieces is fetched whole first. It starts once 0.25 s is decoded; when its audio runs out (a slow network) it is `buffering`, silent, and plays on once 1 s is decoded. Loops are gapless and exact to the sample; `fade` ramps its gain as a sound's. In a browser streams start with the page's audio (the player's first press). Natively a stream decodes on a thread of its own; in a browser in the game's worker between its calls, so a call running longer than about 3 s makes it wait.

### StreamState

*type*

```ts
export type StreamState =
  | "loading"
  | "playing"
  | "paused"
  | "buffering"
  | "ended"
  | "stopped"
  | "failed";
```

Where a stream stands: `loading` until first heard, `playing`, `paused`, `buffering` (its audio ran out; it waits, silent), and finally `ended` (the file's end, without a loop), `stopped` (`stop()`) or `failed` (see `error`).

*interface*

```ts

```

- `bus?: Bus;`

  Default `"music"`.

- `gain?: number;`

  0–16 (default 1).

- `pan?: number;`

  −1 (left) .. 1 (right); omitted: the file's own channels.

- `loop?: boolean;`

- `loopStart?: number;`

  Seconds (default 0): where a loop starts again.

- `loopEnd?: number;`

  Seconds (default the file's end): where a loop turns; past `loopStart`.

- `start?: number;`

  Seconds into the file to start at (default 0).

- `paused?: boolean;`

  Wait for `play()` (default false: it plays as soon as it can).

### AudioStream

*class*

Music decoded as it plays (`stream`).

```ts

```

- `#private;`
- `private constructor();`
- `readonly path: string;`
- `readonly state: StreamState;`

- `readonly position: number;`

  Seconds into the file the player hears (through loops and seeks; where it starts until it is heard).

- `readonly duration: number;`

  Seconds; NaN until the file's last page was read (at once for a file on the device, early for one fetched in pieces).

### stream

*function*

```ts
export function stream(path: string, options?: StreamOptions): AudioStream;
```

Streams a package or remote file (a `NotFoundError` for one the package does not have, a TypeError for a bad path or option, a RangeError past 4 streams or the game's sounds). What the file holds is known only as it is read: one that cannot play fails later (`failed`). Declare `engine.minor=14`.

## The synthesis graph (Web Audio subset)

Names and semantics follow Web Audio for the supported subset. Times are seconds of `context.currentTime` (the mixer's clock, rendered in 128-frame quanta); times before now act now; negative times throw a RangeError, non-finite values a TypeError. Bounds: min(`voices`, 256) nodes, 1,024 connections, 1,024 automation events per parameter and 16,384 in all, curves of at most 65,536 values, 32 MiB of buffers (4,096 at most) and 32 MiB of delay lines, 256 periodic waves, and an estimated render cost of 20,000 units at 48 kHz (less above): a node costs gain 5, constant source 4, stereo panner 5, oscillator 20, buffer source 40, biquad 28, delay 25 (since API\_MINOR 37 panner 12 and the listener 2), and from its first ramp, target, curve or parameter connection on 20, 14, 75, 210, 42, 280 and 42 (40 and 20); each connection 2: past one a RangeError. An automation event counts until the clock passes it, except that a setValue or setTarget (`value =` included) supersedes a setValue or setTarget right before it at the same time, which could no longer affect any value: so `setTargetAtTime(v, currentTime, tc)` once a frame holds one event while the clock stands still (a browser's audio before the page's first press), but events at different future times still fill the budget meanwhile. Not supported: channel count settings (buffers are mono or stereo), wave shapers, convolvers, compressors, analysers, 3D panners and listeners before API\_MINOR 37 (`PannerNode`, `context.listener`; HRTF renders as equal-power), IIR filters, channel splitters and mergers, worklets and media nodes; offline contexts before API\_MINOR 37 (`OfflineAudioContext`); `AudioParam.value` reads the last value set, not the automation's progress.

*type*

export type AutomationRate = "a-rate" | "k-rate";
```

Without it, Web Audio's lifetime rules hold: a source that ended is freed by itself, and any other node is freed once nothing connects into it (or only freed nodes do) and the script holds no reference to it (it was garbage collected).

### PannerNode

*class*

Since API\_MINOR 37 (`SPATIAL_AUDIO_MINOR`; `createPanner` throws a TypeError before): Web Audio's PannerNode, a mono or stereo input placed in 3D against the context's `listener`, output in stereo: equal-power panning by the source's azimuth (behind folds to the front, as the specification has it), times its distance model's gain and its cone's, the specification's formulas with Chromium's bound (the distance clamped to `maxDistance` in the inverse and exponential models too). With the player's Spatial sound off it keeps that gain and drops only the panning (centered, as a source straight ahead): the setting is the player's, so the graph's panners honour it as placed sounds do; an offline context renders as set. The position, orientation and the listener are taken once a render quantum (128 frames: their automation's value at its first frame), as Firefox does. Positions are a-rate AudioParams (automatable; connections into them modulate as usual). Render cost 12, automated 40.

### AudioListener

*class*

Since API\_MINOR 37 (`SPATIAL_AUDIO_MINOR`): Web Audio's AudioListener (`context.listener`, an offline context's own): where every PannerNode, and every sound played with a `position`, is heard from. Positioned clips follow the value each was last set to, or the value its last ramp, target or set goes to. starhermit: scene's `AudioListener` (three.js's) moves it with a camera.

### AudioContext

*class*

The game's one synthesis graph: `new AudioContext()` returns `context` (options are ignored), so web code ports unchanged.

```ts

```

- `#private;`
- `constructor(options?: { latencyHint?: string; sampleRate?: number });`

- `readonly currentTime: number;`

  Seconds of mixer time, as the mixer's clock reads now (its last report, a few frames old, plus the time since; also in the first frames after the page or window was hidden): a source started at `currentTime` starts at once, one at `currentTime + k` k seconds later. It stands still while `state` is `"suspended"`.

- `readonly sampleRate: number;`

- `readonly state: "running" | "suspended";`

  `"suspended"` while the game's audio waits to start: in a browser, until the player's first press on the page that the browser counts as a gesture (Web Audio's autoplay policy: a click, a tap or a key, but not a modifier key alone; until then each press tries again); `"running"` once it runs, and natively from the start. Clips, sounds, streams and the graph wait meanwhile.

- `onstatechange: ((event: { type: "statechange" }) => void) | null;`

  Fires when `state` changes (in a browser, as audio starts); natively never.

- `addEventListener(type: "statechange", listener: (event: { type: "statechange" }) => void): void;`
- `removeEventListener(type: "statechange", listener: (event: { type: "statechange" }) => void): void;`

  The effects bus (what web code's `destination` becomes).

Since API\_MINOR 37 (`AUDIO_NOISE_MINOR`; ignored before) `seed`, a whole number of at most 2^53 − 1 (RangeError), gives the same samples for the same seed, length and sample rate in every run and on every platform; without one the noise differs each time.

  Decodes a package file, read without waiting for it (see `PackageFiles`); rejects as `loadClip` does.

- `resume(): Promise<void>;`

  Resolves once audio runs: at once unless it waits to start, else with the page's first press, as `statechange` fires (a game cannot start audio itself: the press does).

- `suspend(): Promise<void>;`

  Resolves at once; the graph runs while the game does.

### OfflineAudioContext

*class*

Since API\_MINOR 37 (`OFFLINE_AUDIO_MINOR`; the constructor throws a TypeError before): Web Audio's OfflineAudioContext, for pads, beds, ticks and other procedural sound a game bakes once and plays as a clip. Its nodes are made as `context`'s are, with the same bounds (counted per context: at most 256 nodes alive, or `engine.limits.voices` if lower, else a RangeError "audio node limit reached"; 1,024 connections), and connect only to its own nodes and buses (`InvalidAccessError` across contexts); every bus of an offline context is its output. `startRendering()` renders natively, by the mixer's own synthesis code, a share of the render each frame as frames begin (counted in the graph's estimated cost, so a render settles at the same frame in every run; a 4 s pad of a few nodes takes a frame or two), and settles with an AudioBuffer. The samples are the bits the live graph gives for the same graph and sample rate at unity volume, with its sources' times from 0, except that they are not clamped to ±1. `createClip(buffer)` makes it a clip. At most 16 offline contexts at once that have not finished rendering (RangeError); a context gives up its place as its render completes, so one context per stem rendered in turn never reaches it. Finished contexts not yet collected: at most 256, holding no more than 16 graphs' budgets in all (RangeError). Each renders at most 8,388,608 samples (channels × length; RangeError).

```ts
export class OfflineAudioContext { … }
```

- `#private;`

- `constructor(numberOfChannels: number, length: number, sampleRate: number);`

  1 or 2 channels, a length of at least one frame, 3–768 kHz (rounded to a whole hertz): `NotSupportedError` otherwise.

- `constructor(options: { numberOfChannels?: number; length: number; sampleRate: number });`
- `readonly length: number;`
- `readonly numberOfChannels: number;`

- `readonly currentTime: number;`

  Seconds rendered: 0 until `startRendering()`, `length / sampleRate` once done.

- `readonly state: "suspended" | "running" | "closed";`

  `"suspended"` until `startRendering()`, `"running"` while it renders, `"closed"` once done.

- `readonly destination: AudioBusNode;`

  Its output (every bus of an offline context is).

- `bus(name: Bus): AudioBusNode;`

- `oncomplete: ((event: { type: "complete"; renderedBuffer: AudioBuffer }) => void) | null;`
